mx-b09-s01: ¿Tengo que validar el boleto? ¿Tengo que hacer transbordo?
mx-b09-n07: B09 complete. Destination, boleto, validation rule, platform, transfer, confirm the vehicle — the sequence is your job.
mx-b09-q-i: A traveller needs local transport to the Historic Centre. Listen for the two different destination checks and the two obligations discovered in between.
mx-b09-q02: Sí, pero tiene que hacer transbordo.
mx-b09-q03: Un boleto para el centro, por favor. ¿Tengo que validar el boleto?
mx-b10-n01: B10 is silent — no pronouncing, no copying. Just recognise a sign and move: enter, exit, pull, push, queue, toilets, time, stop.
mx-b10-n02: At a divided doorway, choose the flow first — entrada in, salida out. Let the arrow and people confirm it, don't stop to translate.
mx-b10-n03: On a manual door, jale pulls toward you, empuje pushes away. Read it before your hand reaches the handle.
mx-b10-n04: Fila marks where waiting begins, taquilla is the ticket window. If a queue leads there, join the back, don't walk to the glass.
mx-b10-n05: Both signs lead to the toilets — follow the pictogram and arrow. No sign? Fall back to B08's location question.
mx-b10-n06: Horario shows the hours for that place specifically — check today's range. Cerrado ends it: change time or place.
mx-b10-n07: Último acceso is the deadline to enter, not closing time. Solo personal is a boundary — stop, find the public route.
mx-b10-n08: B10 complete. Entrance, exit, pull, push, queue, toilets, hours, last entry, staff only — sign to decision to body.
mx-b10-q-i: You are moving through a terminal and a public building. Hear the six sign surfaces once, then choose the action each one controls.
mx-b11-n01: A taquería might have table, counter or cashier service — don't guess the ritual. First make your group visible.
mx-b11-p01: You and one companion arrive in the afternoon. Greet the person receiving customers and state your group size. Speak now.
mx-b11-n02: Group size doesn't promise a seat — ask for the table itself: a table for two.
mx-b11-p02: The room is busy and no one has pointed to a seat yet. Ask whether there is a table for the two of you. Speak now.
mx-b11-n03: A gesture toward a table can still leave doubt — confirm the seat before sitting, cheaper than relocating later.
mx-b11-p03: You reach the open table indicated at the back. Confirm that you should sit there. Speak now.
mx-b11-n04: Discover where the order begins — one question covers both table and counter service, aquí or en la mesa.
mx-b11-p04: There is a cashier near the entrance and menus on the tables. Ask where your order should start. Speak now.
mx-b11-r04: Aquí en la caja, por favor.
mx-b11-n05: Channel known. Buy time with the first drink while you check the food — just keep un agua mineral as one chunk.
mx-b11-p05: At the correct ordering point, ask for one sparkling water before choosing food. Speak now.
mx-b11-n06: Anything else doesn't force the taco decision — por ahora closes this round while keeping the menu open.
mx-b11-t06: Eso es todo por ahora, gracias.
mx-b11-p06: You have the first drink but still need time with the menu. Close this round without closing the whole meal. Speak now.
mx-b11-s01: ¿Ordeno aquí o en la mesa? Un agua mineral, por favor. Eso es todo por ahora, gracias.
mx-b11-n07: B11 complete. Group visible, table, seat confirmed, ordering channel, first drink, close for now — the room is working for you.
mx-b11-q-i: Two travellers enter a busy taquería. Listen for the moment when the service format becomes clear and for the phrase that leaves the food order open.
mx-b11-q01: Buenas tardes. Somos dos. ¿Hay mesa para dos?
mx-b11-q03: ¿Nos sentamos aquí? ¿Ordeno aquí o en la mesa?
mx-b11-q04: Sí, adelante. Aquí en la caja, por favor.
mx-b11-q05: Un agua mineral, por favor. Eso es todo por ahora, gracias.
mx-b12-n01: The menu gives you the base — six small controls change the result. Start with quantity and the item as listed.
mx-b12-t01: Quería dos tacos al pastor, por favor.
mx-b12-p01: At the cashier from B11, order two of the rotating-spit tacos named on the menu. Speak now.
mx-b12-n02: Todo isn't a fixed list — answer with what you actually want. Con adds the ingredients you name.
mx-b12-p02: For the first taco, accept the chopped onion and cilantro offered at this counter. Speak now.
mx-b12-n03: Second taco, different build. The frame is sin plus an ingredient — not an allergy guarantee, B13 covers that.
mx-b12-t03: El otro sin cebolla, por favor.
mx-b12-p03: Your companion wants the second taco without the chopped onion. Change only that taco. Speak now.
mx-b12-n04: Keep the salsa reversible — aparte puts it beside the taco, so you control the first taste yourself.
mx-b12-p04: Ask for the salsa in a separate small container, not poured over either taco. Speak now.
mx-b12-n05: Colour doesn't reliably signal heat — ask which one's milder and follow the gesture to this batch.
mx-b12-p05: Two unlabelled salsas are beside the tacos. Ask which one is less spicy. Speak now.
mx-b12-n06: Más asks for one visible extra, not a bigger portion overall — name the thing, like the lime.
mx-b12-p06: The tray has one lime wedge for two tacos. Ask for more lime. Speak now.
mx-b12-n07: The same sin frame works on drinks — name it, remove the ice. Preference, not a health claim.
mx-b12-t07: Una limonada sin hielo, por favor.
mx-b12-p07: Add one lemonade but ask for it without ice. Speak now.
mx-b12-s01: Uno con cebolla y cilantro. El otro sin cebolla. La salsa aparte. Más limón. Una limonada sin hielo.
mx-b12-n08: B12 complete. Base order, con adds, sin removes, aparte keeps salsa reversible, más adds — allergy gets its own route next.
mx-b12-q-i: A pair orders two tacos from the same base but wants different toppings. Listen for the return question and for every control that follows.
mx-b12-q01: Quería dos tacos al pastor, por favor.
mx-b12-q03: Uno con cebolla y cilantro. El otro sin cebolla, por favor.
mx-b12-q04: La salsa aparte, por favor. ¿Cuál salsa pica menos?
mx-b12-q06: Más limón, por favor. Una limonada sin hielo.
mx-b13-n01: Yesterday's request was reversible. Today preference becomes allergy — the tool is a warning plus a written card.
mx-b13-p01: Recall B12. Ask for the salsa on the side. Speak now.
mx-b13-n02: Freeze the warning — don't soften grave or swap alergia for a preference. This uses peanut; your real card names your own allergen.
mx-b13-t01: Tengo una alergia grave al cacahuate.
mx-b13-p02: Before ordering, state the severe peanut allergy without adding a long explanation. Speak now.
mx-b13-p03: The server asks which food. Say that you cannot eat anything containing peanut. Speak now.
mx-b13-t02: No puedo comer nada que contenga cacahuate.
mx-b13-n03: Speech opens it; the card carries the exact warning to the kitchen. A nod at the table isn't kitchen confirmation.
mx-b13-t03: ¿Puede mostrarle esta tarjeta a la persona que prepara la comida?
mx-b13-p04: Place the allergy card in the server's hand and ask for it to reach the person preparing the food. Speak now.
mx-b13-r02: Voy a preguntarle a la cocina.
mx-b13-n04: Ingredient lists are half the question — shared oil, surfaces and utensils can carry it too. Ask the concrete path.
mx-b13-t04: ¿Se prepara en la misma superficie o con los mismos utensilios?
mx-b13-p05: The server returns but has only checked the ingredient list. Ask about the same surface or utensils. Speak now.
mx-b13-n05: That honest answer isn't a service failure — it's the information you needed. Don't bargain; end the order and leave.
mx-b13-t05: Entonces no voy a comer aquí.
mx-b13-p06: The kitchen uses the same surface. Protect the decision: say you will not eat here. Speak now.
mx-b13-n06: Uncertainty gets the same decision — can't confirm it, thank them and don't risk it. Keep your medication and plan accessible.
mx-b13-t06: Gracias por decírmelo. No voy a arriesgarme.
mx-b13-p07: The answer is 'I'm not sure.' Thank the person for saying so and refuse the risk. Speak now.
mx-b13-s01: Tengo una alergia grave al cacahuate. ¿Puede mostrarle esta tarjeta a la persona que prepara la comida? ¿Se prepara en la misma superficie o con los mismos utensilios?
mx-b13-n07: B13 complete. Preference is reversible, allergy isn't — warning, card, surface question, leave if unsafe.
mx-b13-q-i: The kitchen gives an honest answer about a shared surface. Listen for the warning, the concrete preparation question and the safe decision.
mx-b13-q01: Tengo una alergia grave al cacahuate.
mx-b13-q03: No puedo comer nada que contenga cacahuate.
mx-b13-q04: ¿Puede mostrarle esta tarjeta a la persona que prepara la comida?
mx-b13-q05: Voy a preguntarle a la cocina.
mx-b13-q06: ¿Se prepara en la misma superficie o con los mismos utensilios?
mx-b13-q08: Entonces no voy a comer aquí.
mx-b14-n01: Recall the airport payment question — bring it here too, but don't let the terminal outrun the bill.
mx-b14-p01: Recall B06. Before ordering, ask whether you can pay by card. Speak now.
mx-b14-n02: Meal's done. The frame here is ¿me trae, plus whatever you want brought — starting with the bill.
mx-b14-p02: The plates are clear but no bill has arrived. Ask for it. Speak now.
mx-b14-n03: Prices should show in pesos, taxes included. No need to catch spoken numbers — ask to see it if it runs past your ear.
mx-b14-p03: The bill has several lines. Ask for the final amount. Speak now.
mx-b14-p04: You did not catch the amount. Do not guess or practise arithmetic aloud; ask to see it. Speak now.
mx-b14-n04: Your finger stops on an unfamiliar line — don't accuse, don't pay yet. Ask what it is, and ask for removal if unauthorised.
mx-b14-p05: There is an extra line on the bill. Point to it and ask what it is. Speak now.
mx-b14-t05: No autoricé este cargo. ¿Puede quitarlo, por favor?
mx-b14-p06: The server says the unrequested line is the tip. State that you did not authorise it and ask for removal. Speak now.
mx-b14-n05: Removing that line doesn't forbid a voluntary tip — choose your amount after correction, no fixed percentage.
mx-b14-t06: Quiero agregar esta cantidad de propina.
mx-b14-p07: The corrected bill is in front of you. Show the amount you chose on your phone and say you want to add that amount as a tip. Speak now.
mx-b14-n06: Now the total is what you approved. Bring the terminal, compare its screen to the corrected bill, then pay.
mx-b14-p08: The corrected bill is ready and you are keeping the card with you. Ask for the terminal. Speak now.
mx-b14-n07: Close the loop with evidence — ask for the receipt and keep it. It's the last checkable artifact in the scene.
mx-b14-t08: ¿Me puede dar el recibo, por favor?
mx-b14-p09: Payment went through. Ask for the receipt before you leave. Speak now.
mx-b14-s01: ¿Me trae la cuenta, por favor? ¿Cuál es el total? ¿Qué es este cargo? ¿Me trae la terminal, por favor?
mx-b14-n08: B14 complete. Bill before terminal, total visible, unknown line questioned, your tip chosen, receipt kept.
mx-b14-q-i: A traveller receives a bill with an extra tip line before the card terminal arrives. Listen for the review sequence and the amount that is actually authorised.
mx-b14-q05: No autoricé este cargo. ¿Puede quitarlo, por favor?
mx-b14-q07: Quiero agregar esta cantidad de propina. ¿Me trae la terminal, por favor?
mx-b15-n01: Recall B14's receipt — a shop receipt may need to travel back with the product. Ask for it again here.
mx-b15-p01: Recall B14. The card payment is complete. Ask for the receipt. Speak now.
mx-b15-c01: ¿Me puede dar el recibo, por favor?
mx-b15-n02: At a shop, point before you name — esta camisa makes one visible item the question, price included.
mx-b15-p02: A shirt has no visible price. Point to it and ask the cost. Speak now.
mx-b15-n03: The frame is ¿tiene, plus the thing you want. The tag says your size; the garment is the evidence.
mx-b15-p03: The shirt on the rack is tight across the shoulders. Ask for a larger size. Speak now.
mx-b15-p04: The larger shirt is in your hand. Ask whether you can try it on. Speak now.
mx-b15-r03: Sí. Los probadores están al fondo.
mx-b15-n04: Second shirt hangs loose — don't translate a size chart, just ask for the direction: una talla más chica.
mx-b15-p05: The shirt now hangs too loose. Ask for one size smaller. Speak now.
mx-b15-n05: Third size works — close it with me llevo esta: this one, not a catalogue of options.
mx-b15-p06: This size fits and you want the shirt in your hand. Say you will take this one. Speak now.
mx-b15-n06: Fit isn't a defect — don't assume the exchange rule. Before paying, ask if you can change it, and how many days you get.
mx-b15-t06: ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda?
mx-b15-p07: Before paying, ask whether the shirt can be exchanged later if the fit is wrong. Speak now.
mx-b15-r06: Sí, con el recibo y la etiqueta.
mx-b15-p08: The store accepts the exchange with receipt and tag, but you still need the deadline. Ask how many days you have. Speak now.
mx-b15-n07: Next morning, the fit is wrong under real movement. Tag attached, receipt in hand — ask for another size.
mx-b15-p09: You return with the shirt. Ask to exchange it for another size. Speak now.
mx-b15-p10: The clerk asks for the receipt and tag. Put both on the counter and answer. Speak now.
mx-b15-s01: ¿Cuánto cuesta esta camisa? ¿Me la puedo probar? ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda? Quiero cambiarla por otra talla.
mx-b15-n08: B15 complete. Price visible, fit tested, sizes by direction, exchange policy asked before paying, receipt and tag kept.
mx-b15-q-i: A traveller tries three sizes, asks the exchange rule before paying and returns with the two artifacts the store requested.
mx-b15-q02: Sí. Los probadores están al fondo.
mx-b15-q03: ¿La puedo cambiar si no me queda?
mx-b15-q04: Sí, con el recibo y la etiqueta.
mx-b16-n01: Recall B04's portable reservation — open it here with your name, then improve the room before the number's printed.
mx-b16-p01: The receptionist looks up from the screen. State that you have a reservation under the name Morgan. Speak now.
mx-b16-c01: Tengo una reservación a nombre de Morgan.
mx-b16-n02: Room's not assigned yet — ask for the outcome, not a room number: una habitación más silenciosa.
mx-b16-p02: Before the key is issued, ask whether a quieter room is available. Speak now.
mx-b16-r02: Sí, tengo una lejos del elevador.
mx-b16-n03: Quiet's answered. If height matters too, ask separately so they can tell you what's actually available.
mx-b16-t02: ¿Tiene una habitación en un piso alto?
mx-b16-p03: The quiet room is available. Ask whether it can also be on a high floor. Speak now.
mx-b16-n04: Now ask about late checkout — it's availability and policy, not a guarantee, and may come with a limit or charge.
mx-b16-p04: Your flight leaves late tomorrow. Ask whether a later checkout is possible. Speak now.
mx-b16-r04: Sí, hasta las dos, con un cargo adicional.
mx-b16-p05: Late checkout is available with an extra charge. Ask its cost before accepting. Speak now.
mx-b16-n05: Upstairs, the AC doesn't start. Name the object and the failure — one clean sentence gets maintenance moving.
mx-b16-p06: The room is quiet, but the air conditioner will not start. Report the observable failure. Speak now.
mx-b16-n06: A promise without a time leaves you waiting — ask when someone can check it, and turn the repair into a checkpoint.
mx-b16-p07: Reception will send maintenance. Ask when they can check the unit. Speak now.
mx-b16-n07: Checkpoint passed, still broken. Escalate once: state it's still failing and ask for another room — earned, not a threat.
mx-b16-t07: Sigue sin funcionar. Necesito otra habitación, por favor.
mx-b16-p08: Maintenance checked the unit, but it still does not work. State that and ask for another room. Speak now.
mx-b16-r07: Entiendo. Le voy a cambiar la habitación.
mx-b16-s01: ¿Hay una habitación más silenciosa? ¿Es posible salir más tarde mañana? El aire acondicionado no funciona. Necesito otra habitación, por favor.
mx-b16-n08: B16 complete. Reservation, quiet, high floor, late checkout checked, defect named, repair timed, room changed if needed.
mx-b16-q-i: A traveller improves the room before assignment, then reports one defect and escalates only after the promised repair checkpoint fails.
mx-b16-q02: Sí, tengo una lejos del elevador.
mx-b16-q07: Sigue sin funcionar. Necesito otra habitación, por favor.
mx-b17-n01: The one openly defensive part of the module — mostly small, a headache, a question. But these four moves scale to a real emergency.
mx-b17-p01: At the pharmacy counter, name the pain before asking for anything. Speak now.
mx-b17-n02: Duration is the first thing a pharmacist needs, not a diagnosis — keep it to one clean answer.
mx-b17-p02: The pharmacist asks since when. Answer with one clean phrase: since yesterday. Speak now.
mx-b17-r02: Le recomiendo este para el dolor.
mx-b17-n03: Since 2010, pharmacies can't sell antibiotics without a Mexico-licensed prescription — a foreign one won't work here either. Ask first.
mx-b17-p03: Before you take anything to the till, ask whether this medication needs a prescription. Speak now.
mx-b17-n04: One more filter, connecting to B13 — the allergy sentence applies at the pharmacy counter too.
mx-b17-t04: Tengo una alergia. ¿Tiene algo sin aspirina?
mx-b17-p04: You cannot take aspirin. Say so and ask for an alternative. Speak now.
mx-b17-n05: Now the scale-up — same four moves, but the object is a real emergency and the phone is the counter.
mx-b17-p05: Someone next to you has collapsed. Call and say you need an ambulance. Speak now.
mx-b17-n06: 911 covers the whole country — ambulance, police, fire, one number. Give the address you made portable in B04.
mx-b17-p06: Give your location using the hotel name and room number. Speak now.
mx-b17-t06: Estoy en el hotel, en la habitación trescientos cinco.
mx-b17-s01: Me duele la cabeza. ¿Necesito receta para este medicamento? Necesito una ambulancia.
mx-b17-n07: B17 complete. Name it, timeframe, ask the constraint — receta, alergia. If it scales up: 911, ambulance, the address.
mx-b17-q-i: A traveller describes a headache at the pharmacy, checks the prescription rule and later calls for real help. Listen for the same four-move pattern at two different scales.
mx-b17-q01: Me duele la cabeza. Desde ayer.
mx-b17-q02: Le recomiendo este para el dolor.
mx-b17-q05: Necesito una ambulancia. Estoy en el hotel, en la habitación trescientos cinco.
mx-b18-n01: Last morning. Close the room, store the bag properly, thank the people who made it work — leave with a sentence, not silence.
mx-b18-r01: Buenos días. ¿Todo bien con la habitación?
mx-b18-p01: Reception asks how the room was. Confirm and say you're here to check out. Speak now.
mx-b18-t01: Todo bien, gracias. Vengo a hacer el check-out.
mx-b18-n02: Flight's late tonight, checkout clock doesn't care — don't carry the bag all day, ask the one question that solves it.
mx-b18-t02: ¿Puedo dejar mi maleta aquí hasta la tarde?
mx-b18-p02: Your flight isn't until tonight. Ask whether you can leave your suitcase here until the afternoon. Speak now.
mx-b18-r03: Sí, claro. Aquí tiene su comprobante.
mx-b18-n03: Hold onto that comprobante — same logic as B14 and B15's receipts, the paper that gets your bag back without argument.
mx-b18-r04: ¿Le gustaría dejar alguna propina para la camarista?
mx-b18-n04: Genuinely voluntary, unlike B14's automatic line — commonly a small daily amount left visibly, but the choice is yours.
mx-b18-t03: Sí, ya la dejé en la habitación.
mx-b18-p03: You already left a tip in the room this morning. Confirm that. Speak now.
mx-b18-n05: Last piece, one sentence — not a review, just the same close you used all module: thanks, and see you.
mx-b18-r05: Gracias por su visita. Que tenga buen viaje.
mx-b18-p04: Close the stay the way you closed every counter this trip. Thank them and say goodbye. Speak now.
mx-b18-s01: Vengo a hacer el check-out. ¿Puedo dejar mi maleta aquí hasta la tarde? Muchas gracias. Hasta luego.
mx-b18-n06: B18 complete, básico with it. Check out, claim ticket, tip on your terms, close with the same words you opened with.
mx-b18-q-i: A traveller checks out hours before a night flight. Listen for the storage ticket, the voluntary tip and the final goodbye.
mx-b18-q01: Todo bien, gracias. Vengo a hacer el check-out.
mx-b18-q02: ¿Puedo dejar mi maleta aquí hasta la tarde?
mx-b18-q03: Sí, claro. Aquí tiene su comprobante.
mx-b18-q04: ¿Le gustaría dejar alguna propina para la camarista?
mx-b18-q05: Sí, ya la dejé en la habitación.
mx-i01-n01: Today's decision isn't a phrase — it's a time. What hour you sit down decides which room you eat in.
mx-i01-n02: Six in the evening, the whole comedor is yours — every table free, nobody else in the room.
mx-i01-n03: Nothing's wrong. La comida runs one to three — by six, the city already ate. What's open now runs on tourist hours.
mx-i01-p01: You want to know when this place is genuinely busy. Ask what time la comida is usually served here. Speak now.
mx-i01-t01: ¿A qué hora sirven la comida aquí?
mx-i01-r02: De una a tres, más o menos.
mx-i01-n04: Now the other end of the day — cena isn't a second comida, it's later and lighter, sometimes just a stall snack.
mx-i01-t02: Para la cena, algo ligero está bien.
mx-i01-p02: It's evening and you're not looking for a full meal. Say something light is fine for dinner. Speak now.
mx-i01-n05: The move: want the room the city eats in? Comida, one to three. Just want something before bed? Cena after six, no problem.
mx-i01-r03: ¿Va a comer aquí o solo va de paso?
mx-i01-p03: You've arrived right in the middle of la comida. Say you'd like to eat, here, now. Speak now.
mx-i01-t03: Sí, quiero comer aquí, por favor.
mx-i01-s01: ¿A qué hora sirven la comida aquí? Para la cena, algo ligero está bien.
mx-i01-n06: I01 complete. Comida owns one to three, cena is lighter after six — an empty room at six is the clock, not a warning.
mx-i01-q-i: A traveller walks into an empty comedor at six in the evening and asks when it actually fills up.
mx-i01-q02: ¿A qué hora sirven la comida aquí?
mx-i01-q03: De una a tres, más o menos.
mx-i01-q04: Para la cena, algo ligero está bien.
mx-i02-n01: A busy counter often has no formal line — whoever makes eye contact and speaks up gets served next, not whoever waits quietly.
mx-i02-n02: Fourth person deep at a busy stand, no line, everyone talking over everyone. The cook glances up — this half-second matters.
mx-i02-n03: That question is your opening — answer immediately, at a normal speaking volume, not a whisper or a shout.
mx-i02-p01: The cook asks who's next. Claim your turn immediately. Speak now.
mx-i02-n04: If two people speak at once and it's unclear who was first, this line settles it without an argument.
mx-i02-p02: Someone else also claims the turn. Say, calmly, that you think you arrived first. Speak now.
mx-i02-n05: The English instinct — 'I was wondering if...' — doesn't read as polite here. It reads as distance, not ready to order.
mx-i02-p03: Order directly, no padding, no apology for existing. Speak now.
mx-i02-t03: Deme dos de pastor, por favor.
mx-i02-s01: Yo sigo, por favor. Creo que yo llegué primero. Deme dos de pastor, por favor.
mx-i02-n06: I02 complete. Yo sigo claims your turn, creo que yo llegué primero defends it, deme plus the item is the whole order.
mx-i02-q-i: A crowded taco stand with no formal line. Listen for how the traveller claims a turn and orders directly.
mx-i02-q04: Deme dos de pastor, por favor.
mx-i03-n01: Some of the best food has no printed menu — just a chalkboard, or nothing, today's comida corrida decided that morning.
mx-i03-r01: Hoy tenemos comida corrida: sopa, guisado y agua.
mx-i03-n02: Comida corrida — like menú del día — is a full fixed lunch, fair price, a few hours around midday.
mx-i03-p01: That's exactly what you want. Say you'll have the comida corrida. Speak now.
mx-i03-t01: Quiero la comida corrida, por favor.
mx-i03-n03: Comida corrida still asks you to choose between two or three set options at each course. You don't need every word — you need one clean choice.
mx-i03-p02: Pick one. Say soup. Speak now.
mx-i03-n04: When there's a longer menu and no comida corrida, this move unlocks the good dish instead of the safe one.
mx-i03-p03: You're not sure what to get. Ask what they recommend. Speak now.
mx-i03-s01: Quiero la comida corrida, por favor. ¿Qué me recomienda?
mx-i03-n05: I03 complete. Comida corrida is the move, fair price, usually the best thing in the room — otherwise, ¿qué me recomienda?
mx-i03-q-i: A fonda with no printed menu. Listen for how the traveller orders the fixed daily lunch and asks for a recommendation elsewhere.
mx-i03-q01: Hoy tenemos comida corrida: sopa, guisado y agua.
mx-i03-q02: Quiero la comida corrida, por favor.
mx-i04-n01: Tonight's decision happens before a drink is ordered: who invited whom. That decides who reaches for the bill later.
mx-i04-r01: Vamos por unas cervezas, yo invito.
mx-i04-n02: Yo invito isn't an offer to refuse — it's who's paying tonight. The expected answer is thanks, not a fight.
mx-i04-p01: A friend says he's inviting. Accept it plainly, with thanks. Speak now.
mx-i04-n03: You're allowed to want the other arrangement — splitting isn't the default, so say so early, before the tab runs.
mx-i04-p02: You'd rather split the bill this time. Say so, before ordering. Speak now.
mx-i04-n04: One more version, for a group sharing a table but not a tab: everyone pays for what they actually had.
mx-i04-p03: Suggest that everyone pays for their own order. Speak now.
mx-i04-n05: Leaving before the rest of the table doesn't need a speech — one line covers the exit.
mx-i04-p04: You're heading out while the others stay. Say goodbye to the table. Speak now.
mx-i04-t04: Ya me voy. Gracias por todo, nos vemos.
mx-i04-s01: ¿Podemos pagar por separado? Cada quien paga lo suyo. Ya me voy. Gracias por todo, nos vemos.
mx-i04-n06: I04 complete. Yo invito means accept it, ¿podemos pagar por separado? if you'd rather split, ya me voy to leave cleanly.
mx-i04-q-i: A night out with friends. Listen for who pays, how splitting is requested, and how to leave the table first.
mx-i04-q01: Vamos por unas cervezas, yo invito.
mx-i04-q04: Ya me voy. Gracias por todo, nos vemos.
mx-i05-n01: Almost every stranger asks some version of the same four or five questions — good news, you can walk in with real answers ready.
mx-i05-p01: Answer with where you're actually from. Speak now.
mx-i05-n02: This one wants a real number, not a philosophy. Keep it short.
mx-i05-p02: Give your real length of stay. Speak now.
mx-i05-r03: ¿Qué te ha gustado más de México?
mx-i05-n03: This question makes it warm, not transactional — a specific answer beats a generic 'everything.'
mx-i05-p03: Give one specific thing you've genuinely liked. Speak now.
mx-i05-t03: Me encantó la comida, sobre todo los tacos.
mx-i05-p04: Say who you're travelling with, or that you're on your own. Speak now.
mx-i05-n04: And if you want out of a conversation, that's fine too — one polite line closes it without rudeness.
mx-i05-p05: You need to get going. Excuse yourself politely. Speak now.
mx-i05-t05: Bueno, fue un gusto. Que le vaya bien.
mx-i05-s01: Soy de Estados Unidos. Diez días, más o menos. Me encantó la comida.
mx-i05-n05: I05 complete. Origin, duration, what you've liked, who you're with — have real answers ready, and know how to leave well too.
mx-i05-q-i: A friendly stranger asks the same handful of questions travellers hear constantly. Listen for the ready answers and the polite exit.
mx-i05-q03: ¿Qué te ha gustado más de México?
mx-i05-q04: Me encantó la comida, sobre todo los tacos.
mx-i06-n01: Everything so far lived in the present — order this, ask that. Today: three verbs that turn yesterday into a story.
mx-i06-n02: Fui — I went. The whole day starts with where you went, and that one word carries the whole sentence.
mx-i06-p01: Say where you went yesterday. Speak now.
mx-i06-n03: Comí — I ate. Same pattern, different verb. The story is building itself one short sentence at a time.
mx-i06-p02: Say what you ate. Speak now.
mx-i06-n04: The verb that closes with feeling: me encantó — literally 'it delighted me,' but it lands like 'I loved it.'
mx-i06-p03: Say you loved it. Speak now.
mx-i06-n05: The conversation swings forward too — no new tense needed, vamos a plus what you'll do covers tomorrow.
mx-i06-p04: Say what you're going to do today. Speak now.
mx-i06-t04: Vamos a ir a la playa.
mx-i06-s01: Fui al mercado. Comí tacos al pastor. Me encantó.
mx-i06-n06: I06 complete. Fui, comí, me encantó make yesterday a story, vamos a covers tomorrow — past and future, not just present.
mx-i06-q-i: Someone asks about yesterday. Listen for the three verbs that carry the whole story.
mx-i06-q02: Fui al mercado. Comí tacos al pastor. Me encantó.
mx-i06-q04: Vamos a ir a la playa.
mx-i07-n01: Two moves today: a genuine compliment and a calm complaint, both said out loud. Specific beats vague, either way.
mx-i07-n02: Your opening. Está buenísimo works, but naming the dish gets a bigger reaction — proof you weren't just being polite.
mx-i07-p01: The food was genuinely excellent. Say so, specifically. Speak now.
mx-i07-r02: Muchas gracias, se lo voy a decir.
mx-i07-n03: Now the other move — something's actually wrong. Name the object and the issue, calmly, no speech attached.
mx-i07-p02: The soup arrived cold. Name the problem, calmly. Speak now.
mx-i07-r03: Perdón, se la cambio ahora mismo.
mx-i07-n04: Disculpe opens it without blame — naming the object and the exact problem is what actually gets it fixed fast.
mx-i07-p03: They fixed it fast. Thank them for taking care of it. Speak now.
mx-i07-s01: El mole está buenísimo. Disculpe, la sopa está fría. Gracias por resolverlo tan rápido.
mx-i07-n05: I07 complete. A specific compliment reaches the cook, disculpe plus the exact problem gets it fixed — precise, not loud.
mx-i07-q-i: A meal with one genuine compliment and one real problem. Listen for how both get handled calmly and specifically.
mx-i08-n01: A home invitation is a real gesture. Three small moves make you a good guest: something small, on time, let the host lead the toast.
mx-i08-r01: ¿Te gustaría cenar en mi casa el sábado?
mx-i08-p01: Accept the invitation warmly. Speak now.
mx-i08-t01: Claro que sí, con mucho gusto.
mx-i08-n02: Don't arrive empty-handed — flowers, wine, a dessert are the norm. Skip yellow flowers, which read as mourning here.
mx-i08-p02: At the door, hand over the small gift you brought. Speak now.
mx-i08-t02: Le traje esto para la casa.
mx-i08-r02: No te hubieras molestado, muchas gracias.
mx-i08-n03: Everything else about time can be relaxed — this isn't. On time for a home invitation reads as respect for the work tonight.
mx-i08-r03: Pasa, siéntete como en tu casa.
mx-i08-p03: Thank them for having you. Speak now.
mx-i08-n04: Glasses fill, the host leads the first toast — you don't invent one. One word is the whole reply.
mx-i08-p04: The host raises a glass. Answer the toast. Speak now.
mx-i08-s01: Claro que sí, con mucho gusto. Le traje esto para la casa. Gracias por invitarme.
mx-i08-n05: I08 complete. Something small, arrive on time — the clock doesn't relax here — let the host lead the toast, salud replies.
mx-i08-q-i: A traveller is invited to dinner at a friend's home. Listen for the gift, the timing, and the toast.
mx-i08-q01: ¿Te gustaría cenar en mi casa el sábado?
mx-i08-q02: Claro que sí, con mucho gusto.
mx-i08-q03: Le traje esto para la casa.
mx-i09-n01: One question opens a different kind of afternoon — not what should I see, but what's actually happening this week.
mx-i09-r01: ¿Qué van a hacer este fin de semana?
mx-i09-n02: Turn the question back around — this gets you into someone's actual plan, not a tourist itinerary.
mx-i09-p01: Ask what's happening in the plaza this weekend. Speak now.
mx-i09-t01: ¿Hay algo en la plaza este fin de semana?
mx-i09-r02: Sí, hay un mercado sobre ruedas los domingos.
mx-i09-n03: A mercado sobre ruedas sets up for one day and moves on — a different rhythm from a fixed tourist market. Ask to go along.
mx-i09-p02: Ask if you can come along with them. Speak now.
mx-i09-r03: Claro, nos vemos a las diez.
mx-i09-n04: Once there, you're not performing tourism — just at the market with everyone else, using the same sentence anyone would.
mx-i09-p03: Ask the price of something at a stall, like any other customer. Speak now.
mx-i09-s01: ¿Hay algo en la plaza este fin de semana? ¿Puedo ir con ustedes?
mx-i09-n05: I09 complete. ¿Hay algo en la plaza? finds what's happening, ¿puedo ir con ustedes? turns it into an invitation.
mx-i09-q-i: A traveller discovers a Sunday roving market by asking a local what's happening, then asks to come along.
mx-i09-q01: ¿Qué van a hacer este fin de semana?
mx-i09-q02: ¿Hay algo en la plaza este fin de semana?
mx-i09-q03: Sí, hay un mercado sobre ruedas los domingos.
mx-i10-n01: Today's real skill isn't the phrases — it's knowing where they belong. Get that right and the rest is easy.
mx-i10-n02: A craft stall with no price tag or register is an invitation to negotiate — a supermarket isn't. Read the room first.
mx-i10-p01: You're at an open craft stall, no price marked. Ask a friendly opening question. Speak now.
mx-i10-n03: Now counter-offer, friendly not aggressive — a conversation, not a demand. Genuine interest gets you further than pressure.
mx-i10-p02: Offer a lower price, warmly. Speak now.
mx-i10-t02: ¿Se lo puedo dejar en trescientos cincuenta?
mx-i10-n04: A friendly back-and-forth commonly lands around thirty percent off the opening price — not a rule, just a rough shape.
mx-i10-n05: If the answer is a flat no, that's the end of it — pushing further sours the exchange. Thank them either way.
mx-i10-p03: The vendor can't go any lower. Thank them warmly, whether or not you buy. Speak now.
mx-i10-s01: ¿Cuál es su mejor precio? ¿Se lo puedo dejar en trescientos cincuenta? Está bien, muchas gracias.
mx-i10-n06: I10 complete. Read the room first — at a stall, ¿cuál es su mejor precio? opens it, a warm gracias closes it either way.
mx-i10-q-i: A traveller bargains for a craft item at an open-air stall, then accepts the final price gracefully.
mx-i10-q03: ¿Se lo puedo dejar en trescientos cincuenta?
mx-a01-n01: Today trains your ear, not your mouth. Fast, informal Mexican Spanish drops sounds constantly — and you already own most of it.
mx-a01-n02: So say nothing for the next few minutes. The exercise today is entirely your ears.
mx-a01-n03: Ten at night, a busy taco stand. Two regulars order back to back, and neither sentence slows down for you.
mx-a01-o01: ¿Me da dos de pastor y uno de bistec, pa' llevar?
mx-a01-n04: You didn't catch that, and your ear is fine — every pattern in it comes slowed down next.
mx-a01-n05: First pattern, and the most common: está shrinks to 'tá. Here it is in full, the way you learned it.
mx-a01-n06: Second: para shrinks to pa' — you asked this exact question in part seventeen, at the pharmacy.
mx-a01-n07: Third: nada shrinks to na' — you said this about a peanut allergy. It matters more than most.
mx-a01-o05: No puedo comer na' que contenga cacahuate.
mx-a01-n08: Fourth, and you'll hear it constantly: pues shrinks to pos, or just pus — a filler word, a small shrug.
mx-a01-n09: One more: the d between two vowels in -ado endings often disappears. Cansado becomes cansao, ocupado becomes ocupao.
mx-a01-n10: None of these are mistakes — it's what relaxed, everyday Mexican Spanish sounds like, everywhere in the country.
mx-a01-n11: The accent shifts by region too — central fast, coastal sing-song, Yucatán Maya-influenced, northern distinct. Expect variety, not one accent.
mx-a01-n12: Back to the taco stand — same two sentences from the start, now with all four patterns in your ears.
mx-a01-n13: You got it. Nothing new went in today — what changed is you can find your sentences with pieces missing.
mx-a01-n14: A01 complete. Está to 'tá, para to pa', nada to na', pues to pos — four erosions over sentences you already built.
mx-a01-q-i: Listen to two regulars ordering fast at a taco stand, then answer about what you heard.
mx-a01-q01: ¿Me da dos de pastor y uno de bistec, pa' llevar?
mx-i01-n07: One more useful check: arrive near the edge of the window, just ask before sitting down.
mx-i01-p04: You arrive at half past two, unsure if it's too late. Ask whether they're still serving comida. Speak now.
mx-i02-p04: The cook asks if that's everything. Close it directly, no padding. Speak now.
mx-i03-p04: The main course also has two options. Choose chicken. Speak now.
mx-i07-p04: The new soup arrives hot. Close the loop with a quick, genuine reaction. Speak now.
mx-i09-p04: They just made room for you in their own weekend. Thank them for the invitation. Speak now.
mx-i10-p03b: Many stalls like this run cash-only. Confirm before you dig for a card. Speak now.
mx-a02-n01: Today is about laughing in the right places. Two of the moves are receptive only — you enjoy them, you don't perform them.
mx-a02-n02: Six people at a table. Someone says something ordinary about a spoon and the table detonates. You missed it entirely.
mx-a02-o01: ¿Y tú qué, no le entras a la cuchara?
mx-a02-n03: That's an albur: an ordinary sentence built so an obscene reading sits inside it. People answer albur with albur.
mx-a02-n04: You won't win that volley, and nobody expects you to. The honest move is to say you missed it and ask.
mx-a02-p01: The table is laughing and you have no idea why. Say so, lightly. Speak now.
mx-a02-o02: Ay, no seas malpensado. Es albur.
mx-a02-n05: Asking made you part of it. Now the other half: what they joke about that surprises visitors.
mx-a02-o03: Nos vemos el dos de noviembre, si es que llego.
mx-a02-n06: Death and hardship are fair game, and so are they. Three things are not: national symbols, the Virgin of Guadalupe, and mothers.
mx-a02-n07: Those land badly from a foreigner even when a local just said worse. That asymmetry is what insider licence means.
mx-a02-p02: Someone made a sharp joke about their own city. Appreciate it without adding your own. Speak now.
mx-a02-n08: And the joke that does land from you: yourself. Your accent, your confusion, your first taco. Self-deprecation travels.
mx-a02-p03: Make the joke about your own Spanish, not about them. Speak now.
mx-a02-t03: Mi español todavía no aguanta el albur.
mx-a02-p04: They teased you back and it was friendly. Take it well, out loud. Speak now.
mx-a02-p05: You want to be able to use the word later. Ask what it means. Speak now.
mx-a02-s01: No le entendí, ¿me explicas? Estuvo buenísimo eso. Mi español todavía no aguanta el albur.
mx-a02-n09: A02 complete. Albur and mother jokes stay receptive. Asking, appreciating and laughing at yourself are yours.
mx-a02-q-i: A table laughs at something a visitor missed, and the visitor handles it well.
mx-a02-q01: ¿Y tú qué, no le entras a la cuchara?
mx-a02-q03: Ay, no seas malpensado. Es albur.
mx-a02-q04: Mi español todavía no aguanta el albur.
mx-a03-n01: Today you stop being a tourist in the conversation — not by knowing more, but by asking better and listening longer.
mx-a03-n02: Someone mentions, in passing, that their grandmother spoke a language they never learned. That sentence is a door.
mx-a03-o01: Mi abuela hablaba náhuatl, pero ya nosotros no.
mx-a03-n03: Mexico built its modern self on two ideas: mestizaje, mixture as the national trait, and a direct line back to Tenochtitlan.
mx-a03-p01: Open the door instead of walking past it. Ask where the family is from. Speak now.
mx-a03-o02: De un pueblo de Puebla, en la sierra.
mx-a03-n04: Notice what you didn't do: you didn't say whether that's sad, or beautiful, or a shame. It isn't yours to grade.
mx-a03-p02: You genuinely didn't know that. Say so plainly, without adding a verdict. Speak now.
mx-a03-n05: In 1992 the Constitution called Mexico pluricultural — officially more than one story. That argument is still live.
mx-a03-o03: Aquí todos somos mestizos, aunque no todos lo digan.
mx-a03-n06: Both sentences get said with total confidence. Your job is not to referee — it's to notice which one you're hearing.
mx-a03-p03: Ask what the place name means, rather than what the politics mean. Speak now.
mx-a03-o04: Es náhuatl. Quiere decir lugar de agua.
mx-a03-n07: Place names are the safest way into this. They're everywhere, people like explaining them, and nobody has to take a position.
mx-a03-p04: Say what you find genuinely good about it — the fact, not the person. Speak now.
mx-a03-t04: Me gusta que se conserve el nombre.
mx-a03-p05: Turn it around and offer something of yours, briefly. Speak now.
mx-a03-t05: En mi familia también se perdió un idioma.
mx-a03-s01: ¿De qué parte es tu familia? No sabía eso. Cuéntame más. ¿Y ese nombre qué significa?
mx-a03-n08: A03 complete. Ask where the family is from, ask what the name means, and say you didn't know. No verdict required from you.
mx-a03-q-i: A conversation about a grandmother’s language opens into something larger.
mx-a03-q01: Mi abuela hablaba náhuatl, pero ya nosotros no.
mx-a03-q03: De un pueblo de Puebla, en la sierra.
mx-a04-n01: Every country has a fault line people joke across and would rather a visitor left alone. Here is how to hear Mexico's.
mx-a04-n02: At a table outside the capital, somebody says chilango with a certain tone. Half the table laughs. One person doesn't.
mx-a04-o01: Ay, ya llegó el chilango a decirnos cómo se hace.
mx-a04-n03: Chilango means someone from Mexico City. Inside the capital it's worn proudly. Outside it, it often carries a sting.
mx-a04-n04: And it runs both ways: calling someone de provincia is the other half of the same insult, meaning unsophisticated.
mx-a04-p01: Skip the labels entirely. Ask the neutral question that lets them name themselves. Speak now.
mx-a04-o02: De Monterrey. Regio de toda la vida.
mx-a04-n05: He named himself, so that word is safe to use back. The root is real: a century of money concentrated in the capital.
mx-a04-p02: Use the word he just gave you, and ask about the place rather than the rivalry. Speak now.
mx-a04-o03: Muy distinto al centro. Más seco, más directo.
mx-a04-n06: Now the move that matters. If someone invites you to blame a region, you can decline without being stiff about it.
mx-a04-p03: You're being asked to pick a side in their argument. Step out of it, lightly. Speak now.
mx-a04-t03: Uy, en esa no me meto.
mx-a04-n07: That works because it's honest. You have no stake, and saying so beats a borrowed opinion.
mx-a04-p04: Redirect to something you actually can speak to: what you liked in both places. Speak now.
mx-a04-t04: Me ha gustado todo lo que he visto, la verdad.
mx-a04-p05: Ask what he'd show you if you went there. Speak now.
mx-a04-s01: ¿De qué parte de México eres? Uy, en esa no me meto. Si voy, ¿qué me enseñarías?
mx-a04-n08: A04 complete. Skip both labels. Ask where they are from, use the word they hand you, and stay out of the argument.
mx-a04-q-i: A regional joke lands at a table and a visitor stays out of it gracefully.
mx-a04-q01: Ay, ya llegó el chilango a decirnos cómo se hace.
mx-a04-q03: De Monterrey. Regio de toda la vida.
mx-a04-q04: Uy, en esa no me meto.
mx-a05-n01: Spanish is not the only language in the room. Today is mostly listening, with one small production move at the end.
mx-a05-n02: At a stall in Yucatán, the woman says something to the man beside her that isn't Spanish, then turns back to you.
mx-a05-n03: Mexico recognises sixty-eight Indigenous languages. Nahuatl has about 1.7 million speakers, the Maya languages over 800,000.
mx-a05-n04: That switch wasn't secrecy. Bilingual people move between languages by who they're addressing.
mx-a05-p01: Ask what language that was — curious, not startled. Speak now.
mx-a05-o02: Es maya. Aquí casi todos lo hablamos.
mx-a05-n05: Now the accents. Central runs fast and clipped, the coast sings, the Yucatán carries Maya rhythm, the north has its own pull.
mx-a05-o04: ¿Qué onda, qué te vas a llevar, pariente?
mx-a05-n06: The one production move: a courtesy word. In the Yucatán, dyos bo'otik is thank you. In Nahuatl country, tlazocamati.
mx-a05-p02: You're in the Yucatán and she just helped you. Thank her in Maya. Speak now.
mx-a05-n07: Say the honest thing back. One word is one word, and claiming more than that is how a nice moment turns awkward.
mx-a05-p03: Correct the compliment, warmly. Speak now.
mx-a05-t03: Solo esa palabra, pero la quería decir bien.
mx-a05-p04: Ask her to teach you one more, and to correct your pronunciation. Speak now.
mx-a05-t04: ¿Me enseña otra? Dígame si lo digo mal.
mx-a05-p05: Close it in Spanish, which is where you actually live. Speak now.
mx-a05-s01: ¿Qué lengua es esa? Solo esa palabra, pero la quería decir bien. ¿Me enseña otra?
mx-a05-n08: A05 complete. Sixty-eight languages, four accents, one courtesy word in the right place — and honesty about it.
mx-a05-q-i: A visitor notices a language switch and handles it with curiosity and honesty.
mx-a05-q03: Es maya. Aquí casi todos lo hablamos.
mx-a06-n01: You will not memorise the Mexican calendar. You will learn two questions that make the calendar tell you itself.
mx-a06-n02: You planned the museum for Monday. The person at the desk is making the face of somebody about to explain a puente.
mx-a06-o01: El lunes hacen puente, joven. Cerramos.
mx-a06-n03: A puente is a holiday moved to Monday so the weekend stretches. Several of the seven national rest days work that way.
mx-a06-p01: Before you commit to any plan, ask the direct question. Speak now.
mx-a06-o02: Sí, y el martes muchos no abren tampoco.
mx-a06-n04: That second half only comes if you ask the follow-up. Official closing and actual closing are different lists.
mx-a06-p02: Ask about this place specifically, not about the country. Speak now.
mx-a06-n05: Now the dates that close things unofficially: Día de Muertos, the 31st to the 2nd. Guadalupe on 12 December. And Semana Santa.
mx-a06-n06: Semana Santa is not a legal holiday and it empties offices and fills every beach. Plan around it or plan into it.
mx-a06-o03: En Semana Santa no encuentras nada, todo se llena.
mx-a06-p03: A holiday is coming and you'd rather be in it than avoid it. Ask what actually happens. Speak now.
mx-a06-o04: Se pone el altar y vamos al panteón en la noche.
mx-a06-n07: That is an answer about a family, not a festival — so the next question decides if you're a spectator or a guest.
mx-a06-p04: Ask whether it's alright for a visitor to go, rather than assuming either way. Speak now.
mx-a06-t04: ¿Está bien si va uno de fuera?
mx-a06-p05: Get the practical detail you'll actually need: what time it starts. Speak now.
mx-a06-s01: ¿El lunes es día festivo? ¿Ustedes van a abrir? ¿Qué se hace aquí ese día?
mx-a06-n08: A06 complete. Ask if it is a holiday, then ask if they are opening. And ask what people do — that turns a closed day around.
mx-a06-q-i: A visitor discovers a long weekend the hard way, then learns the two questions.
mx-a06-q01: El lunes hacen puente, joven. Cerramos.
mx-a06-q03: Sí, y el martes muchos no abren tampoco.
mx-a07-n01: Most of today is hearing. The signals are already being sent — the skill is reading them as information, not mixed messages.
mx-a07-n02: You asked for something. The answer sounded like yes. Forty minutes later you understand it was not a yes.
mx-a07-n03: Refusing a request made in good faith can feel like rejecting the person, so the no arrives as a deferral instead.
mx-a07-o02: Déjame ver y yo te aviso.
mx-a07-n04: Yo te aviso, déjame ver, estamos en contacto. A yes with no time attached is the signal. Don't push — just get the timing.
mx-a07-p01: Turn the soft yes into something checkable, without pressure. Speak now.
mx-a07-o03: Uy, hoy va a estar difícil.
mx-a07-n05: There it is. Difícil is the no, delivered so nobody had to say it. Accept it cleanly and you keep the relationship.
mx-a07-p02: You've understood it's a no. Release them from it, warmly. Speak now.
mx-a07-t02: No se preocupe, así está bien.
mx-a07-n06: Now the body. People stand closer than you may expect, a hand on the arm is ordinary, and eye contact reads as sincere.
mx-a07-n07: So stepping back to restore your usual distance is visible — and it reads as coldness. Worth knowing before you do it.
mx-a07-p03: Reassure them without making it about cultural difference. Speak now.
mx-a07-t03: Todo bien, es que ando cansado.
mx-a07-n08: The last signal: time to go. It rarely arrives as words — it arrives as people standing up, or the talk thinning out.
mx-a07-p04: You've read the room and it's time. Name it yourself, before being told. Speak now.
mx-a07-p05: You're the one deferring this time. Use their own form. Speak now.
mx-a07-t05: Déjame ver y yo te aviso.
mx-a07-s01: ¿Más o menos a qué hora? No se preocupe, así está bien. Bueno, ya no los entretengo.
mx-a07-n09: A07 complete. A yes with no hour is a maybe. Difícil is a no. Closer standing is not pressure, and leaving first is courtesy.
mx-a07-q-i: A soft yes turns out to be a no, and the visitor reads it in time.
mx-a07-q03: Uy, hoy va a estar difícil.
mx-a07-q04: No se preocupe, así está bien.
mx-a08-n01: Last part. The goodbye is not admin — it decides whether there is a next time, and it takes longer than you think.
mx-a08-n02: Bag on your shoulder, door in sight, nine people in the room. In some countries you'd wave from the doorway. Not here.
